_comment: Tolerances for the IDENTITY remap check: target mesh == source mesh, so
remap-then-run must reproduce a plain restart of the same field. Both runs
are the same solver on the same mesh with the same rank layout; the only
difference is that one state travelled through the interpolation path.
The path is not bit-exact by construction. build_up_interp_target_field_thermo
rebuilds h/T/k/sigma/d/mu from (rhoh, d) via the property table, which snaps
the density onto the table manifold and moves it by ~6e-9 relative. That is a
deliberate choice (the remapped state is put back on the equation of state),
and it shows up as a first-step drho/dt transient that has decayed by step 2.
Measured agreement after 20 steps is 9-10 significant digits, so 1e-7 relative
leaves two to three decades of margin while still being four to twelve orders
of magnitude tighter than the O(1) errors a broken remap produces.
Poisson and mass-conservation residuals are absolute-only where their
reproducible content is their magnitude rather than their digits: they sit at
round-off when the projection is consistent, so a relative check on 1e-16
would fail for no physical reason.
